summary: Phase B-2 (Polymorphic Notes + Permission Overrides) regression. Backend: 9/9 pytest cases pass — existing test_notes (CRUD + pin ordering + entity filter + empty body 400 + missing filter 422), test_employees (CRUD + role validation + duplicate email 409 + soft delete + override→effective + role-change refreshes defaults), test_tasks (CRUD + filters), plus 6 NEW extended tests (cross-company isolation on GET/PATCH/DELETE, missing entity_type/entity_id → 400, no bleed across entity types with same id, pinned ordering with two notes, non-dict permission_overrides → 400 for list/str/int/bool, case-insensitive duplicate email). Frontend: /team page + Edit Employee modal fully functional — Details/Permissions/Notes tabs render, Permissions grid shows all 4 product rows (accounting, crm, team, projects), toggling accounting Allow → persists after save & reopen (verified via bg-emerald-600 class after reload). NotesBlock inside employee modal supports add/pin/edit/delete round trip. GlobalTasks button opens drawer with filters mine/overdue/today/done and quickadd form. ProductRail renders 4 product testids. Two blocking issues found (see frontend_issues.ui_bugs) plus one seed-data drift.

ui_bugs.issue: The dashboard WelcomeModal is a fullscreen fixed overlay (z-[900]) whose backdrop intercepts pointer events across the entire viewport, INCLUDING the top-bar/left ProductRail. Attempting to click any [data-testid=product-rail-*] icon on /dashboard yields Playwright errors: '[welcome-modal] subtree intercepts pointer events'. This directly breaks the Phase A-2 core flow ('Product Rail switches between /accounting, /crm, /team, /projects') until a user manually dismisses the modal. The modal auto-reappears on each dashboard visit (Replay welcome). Recommend: (a) constrain click capture to the inner modal card, letting header/rail pointer events through, OR (b) lift ProductRail z-index above z-[900], OR (c) auto-suppress after first dismissal.

Filter buttons for mine/overdue/today/done are wired (data-testid=global-tasks-filter-{k}) but the 'all' filter has no data-testid — the review contract implies a 5th filter tab. Verify whether an 'all' filter should exist in the drawer.

action_items: Fix WelcomeModal backdrop so it does not block ProductRail navigation (Phase A-2 regression). Either restrict pointer-events to the inner card (className adjust) or raise ProductRail z-index above the modal.
Verify whether GlobalTasks drawer should expose an 'all' filter (data-testid=global-tasks-filter-all) alongside mine/overdue/today/done.

Restore seed data: client@axiom.ai per /app/memory/test_credentials.md should own 'Skyward Sparks, LLC' — instead the account now defaults to 'AutoSwitchCo 1786792423' and Skyward Sparks is NOT in that user's company switcher. This impedes reviewer/E2E testing that references Skyward Sparks.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/notes.py list_notes uses required Query(...) for entity_type/entity_id — good; missing filter correctly returns 422. Body validation via HTTPException 400 for empty body and missing entity_* fields is clean.
routes/notes.py has no dedicated GET-by-id endpoint and PATCH/DELETE do not verify author — any member with company access can edit/delete anyone's note. Acceptable for MVP but worth noting.
routes/employees.py get_effective_permissions computes effective = {...defaults, ...overrides}. Correct precedence (overrides win), matches tests.

routes/employees.py permission_overrides accepts arbitrary keys (no whitelist against known products accounting|crm|team|projects). A junk key like {"foo": true} would be persisted and returned in `effective`. Consider whitelisting or ignoring unknown product keys to prevent frontend surprises.

Hard-delete guard in employees.py only checks tasks.assignee_user_id, not employees created without a linked user (user_id is None → task_ref query would still match if any task has assignee_user_id=None which is a match-anything issue for None). Suggest: skip the tasks lookup entirely when doc.user_id is falsy.
Frontend WelcomeModal backdrop pointer-events issue is documented above. Static Tailwind class `z-[900]` on outer wrapper is the root cause.

IMPORTANT: dismiss the WelcomeModal or delete it via JS before interacting with the ProductRail — see UI bug #1. The NotesBlock component code is identical to the one used in the Employee modal (already verified), so functional risk is low even without direct UI hit.
rca of the issue: WelcomeModal (Layout.jsx line 237) wraps its content in a full-viewport fixed div with class 'fixed inset-0 z-[900] bg-slate-900/60 ...' — this outer element captures all pointer events even though ProductRail is visually separate. Since ProductRail's stacking context is below z-[900], every click on the rail is intercepted by the modal backdrop. Fix: apply pointer-events-none to the backdrop and pointer-events-auto to the inner card, or raise the ProductRail container to z-[1000].
